text.p: Austrian insurer EA-Generali said on Tuesday it had agreed with bank Creditanstalt to untangle the two group's cross holdings following the takeover of Creditanstalt by Bank Austria in January this year.
The Italian-controlled insurance group said it had sold its 4.82 voting stake in Creditanstalt to Bank Austria.
In turn, Italy's Assecurazioni Generali, which owns the majority of EA-Generali's shares, had acquired a 2.36 percent voting stake in EA-Generali from Creditanstalt.
The bank currently sells EA-Generali's insurance products over its counters in Austria. Bank Austria currently cooperates with Vienna insurer Wiener Staedtische.

EA-Generali added Assecurazioni Generali would also take over directly or indirectly the remaining EA-Generali shares currently held by Creditanstalt. According to its annual report, the bank owned a total of 9.79 percent of EA-Generali's equity at the end of last year.
EA-Generali and Creditanstalt had "made a decision to untangle their cross-holdings step by step," EA-Generali said.
It added the share parcels would be priced according to a long-term daily average of the shares' prices on the Vienna stock exchange. It gave no further details.
EA-Generali's shares closed at 3,048 schillings on the Vienna bourse on Tuesday, while Creditanstalt's ordinary shares finished the day at 689.85 schillings.

Their two joint units, CA-Generali Versicherungs AG and CA-EA Investment Ges.m.b.H, would undergo a valuation. Creditanstalt would eventually take over CA-Generali, while EA-Generali would take on CA-EA Investment, EA-Generali said.
The future of the cooperation between EA-Generali and Creditanstalt had been unclear since Bank Austria merged with Creditanstalt earlier this year in a deal valued at around 17 billion schillings.
